newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak PM says no crown devaluation considered.
newsitem.headline: Slovak PM says no crown devaluation considered.

text.p: Slovakia is not considering any administrative devaluation of its currency, the crown, Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar was quoted as saying on Monday.
"Despite whatever we've heard from abroad, we are neither planning nor considering a devaluation of the crown," economic daily Narodna Obroda quoted Meciar as saying.
The Slovak crown has been under speculative pressure over the past three weeks but the central bank's moves on local money markets have prevented the currency from suffering any radical decline.

In an attempt to avoid the fate suffered by the Czech crown, which lost nearly 10 percent of its value after a sustained speculative assault and was eventually permitted to float by the Czech National Bank, the Slovak central bank has squeezed liquidity on the interbank market and intervened directly to support the crown.
Meciar also called for people to keep confidence in the Slovak crown and leave their deposits in banks.

The crown has several times touched the floor of its plus/minus 7.0 percent fluctuation band during the run on the currency, but the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) has repeatedly fixed it at levels stronger than -1.0 percent on the depreciation side of mark/dollar basket parity.
Some analysts have said the crown was overvalued at levels close to the NBS fixing and have expected it to depreciate at least within the current fluctuation band.

Analysts have pointed mainly to the fact that Slovakia's strong trade links with the Czech Republic could result in acceleration of Bratislava's trade deficit due to the strength of the Slovak crown against the czech currency.
